results.controlIntent: [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] are used to: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system; and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Prohibit changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
CM-3(1).r4 requires automated mechanisms to: (a) document proposed changes, (b) notify approval authorities and request approval, (c) highlight unapproved changes past a time threshold, (d) **prohibit changes until approvals are received**, (e) document all changes, and (f) notify personnel when approved changes are completed.

Evidence reveals two critical failures:

**Failure 1 — Unapproved hotfix deployment (sub-requirements d & e):**
The UpdateEndpoint event (evidence `1be00bc3`) on 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z deployed config "churn-predictor-v1-hotfix" with no corresponding model registry entry. This means a change was made to the production endpoint with no documented approval — directly violating the requirement to prohibit changes until designated approvals are received and to document all changes.

**Failure 2 — Initial deployment timing ambiguity (sub-requirement d):**
The CreateEndpoint event (evidence `05b25cb1`) at 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z occurred after the registry approval timestamp of 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z (evidence `cd3bd217`), so the initial deployment does follow approval in time. However, the event note flags this as a change-control concern, and there is no evidence of an automated gate (e.g., a pipeline or IAM policy) that *enforced* the approval prerequisite — the deployment could have been made manually at any time.

**Failure 3 — Missing automated mechanism evidence (sub-requirements b, c, f):**
There is no evidence of automated notifications to approval authorities for proposed changes, no evidence of automated alerting for changes pending beyond an organization-defined time period, and no evidence of automated completion notifications to designated personnel. The registry shows a manual approval status field but no automated workflow artifacts.

In summary, the hotfix deployment alone constitutes a clear, documented violation of the "prohibit changes until approved" requirement, and the absence of any automated notification/gate mechanism evidence means multiple sub-requirements of CM-3(1) are unmet.
gaps: No evidence of an automated approval-gate mechanism (e.g., SageMaker Pipeline condition step, IAM deny policy, or EventBridge rule) that would technically prohibit endpoint changes without a registry-approved model package.
No evidence of automated notifications to approval authorities when changes are proposed (CM-3(1)(b)).
No evidence of automated alerting for changes pending approval beyond an organization-defined time period (CM-3(1)(c)).
No evidence of automated completion notifications to designated personnel after approved changes are deployed (CM-3(1)(f)).
No registry entry or approval record for the 'churn-predictor-v1-hotfix' endpoint config used in the March 2026 UpdateEndpoint event.
Human attestation needed to confirm whether any out-of-band approval process existed for the hotfix deployment.
